articles.title: Kay Adams causes huge stir with Super Bowl 61 prediction: “They're killing me”
articles.standfirst: Adams’ Bears-Broncos Super Bowl prediction gets roasted by NFL fans
articles.summary: Adams’ Bears-Broncos Super Bowl prediction gets roasted by NFL fans
articles.body:
NFL host Kay Adams is standing by a Bears-Broncos matchup despite a wave of skepticism, with most of the criticism aimed squarely at Chicago rather than Denver.

Adams knew her Super Bowl LXI prediction was aggressive. What she didn't expect was just how quickly NFL fans would turn it into a debate.

The FanDuel TV host has picked the Chicago Bears to face the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium, a matchup that immediately drew pushback because of how far Adams believes Chicago can go.

“I’m getting killed for my Super Bowl teams,” Adams told Rob Gronkowski.

“I said Bears vs Broncos . But I’m getting crushed and it’s not about the Broncos, which obviously, best defense, maybe Bo Nix can pull it out. Sean Payton. People are really killing me on the Bears.”

Then she put the question directly to Gronkowski : “How bad is my Super Bowl pick?”

Denver is easier to defend

The Broncos are coming off a 14-3 season and a trip to the AFC Championship Game, which makes Adams ’ confidence in Denver easier to understand. She's also been vocal about how highly she rates the roster.

“The [Broncos have the] most complete roster already in the NFL, and then they bring in, which is somehow still being slept on, Jaylen Waddle,” Adams said.

“I cannot for the life of me understand why this team is getting the eighth-longest odds in the conference right now.”

Adams isn't alone in that assessment. ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky has also argued that Denver is being overlooked despite finishing as the AFC’s No.1 seed last season.

“This roster is absolutely loaded,” Orlovsky said. “They are the best team that, for some reason, we are constantly overlooking.”

That makes Chicago the real swing factor in Adams ’ prediction.

Bears pick has fans pushing back

Some fans believe the Bears ’ 2025 success will be difficult to repeat, while others think Chicago is being dismissed too easily.

“The Bears are going to show all y’all that it wasn’t all some mysterious apparition happening last season,” one fan wrote. “They have a top-notch coach with a quarterback that has that clutch gene everyone talks about.”

Another pointed to Caleb Williams ’ late-game play even before Chicago’s recent rise: “I mean year one with Caleb he led a lot of drives late in game that were foiled by terrible coaching decisions,” the fan wrote.

Another fan rejected the idea that last season should simply be written off as a one-off run. “Saying last year was magical without even making the Super Bowl and then saying it doesn’t happen two years in a row is almost hater type talk,” the fan said.

That is ultimately the bet Adams is making. Denver has already shown it can reach the final stages of the AFC race. Chicago still has to prove it belongs in that same category. Adams is betting that 2026 is the year it does.

articles.title: Justin Bieber and Harry Styles the frontrunners for 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show... but there's a major drawback
articles.standfirst: Roc Nation reportedly has two global superstars in mind for SoFi Stadium
articles.summary: Roc Nation reportedly has two global superstars in mind for SoFi Stadium
articles.body:
The Super Bowl halftime show has become as much a global entertainment event as a football spectacle, and the NFL may be aiming particularly high for 2027.

Justin Bieber and Harry Styles are reportedly among the leading names on Roc Nation’s wish list for Super Bowl LXI, which will be played Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

TMZ reports that both artists are high on the list being considered by Roc Nation, the entertainment company founded by Jay-Z that works with the NFL on its live music strategy.

There is, however, an important distinction between being wanted and being booked.

Neither Bieber nor Styles has reportedly been formally approached about performing, and TMZ suggested both could ultimately decline even if offers are made.

That leaves the NFL with an intriguing early shortlist but no confirmed headliner.

Bieber already has experience

Bieber would arrive with relatively recent experience performing around one of the world’s biggest sporting events.

The Canadian singer appeared during halftime entertainment at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, part of a first-of-its-kind show that generated debate because soccer traditionally has a far shorter halftime break than the NFL.

Reaction to Bieber ’s appearance was mixed, including discussion over his song selection, but the setting provided another reminder of the scale of audience he can command. A Super Bowl performance would be very different.

Halftime entertainment is deeply embedded in the NFL’s championship event, and artists frequently use the platform as a way to reach hundreds of millions of viewers while giving their catalog a major commercial boost.

The NFL doesn't traditionally pay its halftime performer a standard appearance fee, although production expenses are covered. The value instead comes from exposure, with streaming numbers, ticket demand and music sales often surging around the performance.

SoFi Stadium adds more expectation

The location only increases the pressure on whoever eventually gets the call. The last Super Bowl held at SoFi Stadium featured a blockbuster halftime lineup of Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, Kendrick Lamar and 50 Cent .

That show became one of the most memorable halftime productions of recent years and set a high bar for the event’s return to Los Angeles.

Styles would bring a different energy, combining his One Direction fan base with a hugely successful solo career. Bieber would offer similar global reach, with a catalog spanning more than a decade of mainstream pop.

The NFL usually announces its halftime performer around late September, meaning a decision could come relatively soon. Until then, Bieber and Styles remain high-profile possibilities rather than actual bookings.

The NFL may know who it wants, but the harder part could be convincing either one to take the stage.
